Bellevue Festivals & Events Incubator Pr.notes: Visit Bellevue does not publish a recipient list, tier table, or per-event amounts for the incubator; the program page (visitbellevue.com) could not be fetched from this session (domain not on allowlist). Aggregate results reported: for 2024, incubator/sponsorship funding supported 20 major events (425business, 2025 annual meeting recap) or 25 festivals, events, conventions and conferences (April 2026 BRTPA packet), generating 26,400 room nights and over $28M direct visitor spending; May 2025 BRTPA minutes cite 16,000 weekend room nights, 26,000 overnight visitors, $28M economic impact for 2024 and an 18,000 room-night goal for 2025. 2025 Visit Bellevue targets: 50K overnight visitors, 24K weekend room nights, $10M new visitor spending, $25M economic impact. March 2026 minutes: the incubator 'typically supports several festivals and community events each year'; some events get multi-year support, and the application process is changing to require annual review. The program is funded by the Bellevue Tourism Promotion Area (Bellevue zone gross budget about $3M/yr, 2025 remittances $2.71M). Events named above are examples cited by Visit Bellevue, not an official award list.

Arts & Culture Project Grants.notes: The city's 2025 allocations list (projects, organizations and artists funded in 2025) is hosted on bellevue.legistar.com, which could not be fetched from this session; the 2026 list above is complete. No Eastside Arts Partnership (operating support) recipient list with amounts was located for the 2025-26 cycle. 'Special projects' is not a current program name; current programs are Project Grants ($3K/$5K/$7K + $1K BelRed bonus), EAP support grants (up to $15K/yr) and Arts & Cultural Facility capital grants. 2026 Project Grants: 31 awards, $187,000, plus 13 BelRed bonuses ($13,000), total $200,000. Project Grant applications for 2027 closed Oct 10, 2026; EAP 2027-28 closed Oct 10, 2026 (next cycle expected fall 2027). Grants are run through bellevuearts.submittable.com.

Cross-Cultural Center Without Walls gran.typical_award: 2026 RFP: single organizations may request $2,500 to $10,000; partnered proposals up to $15,000 combined; no project may exceed $15,000. First (pilot) cohort: 18 orgs/35 events announced May 2024; later reported as 19 orgs/60 events/4,000+ people. The program won 2nd place in the National League of Cities 2024 City Cultural Diversity Awards. The city's Cross-Cultural Center Without Walls Directory lists about 71 organizations but is a service directory, not an award list. Contact: Sara Boyle, DEI Administrator.

Port of Seattle Tourism Marketing Suppor.typical_award: Tier 1 up to $20,000, Tier 2 up to $10,000, each with a 2:1 match (up to 50% of match may be administrative costs). $600,000 per two-year cycle; 2026-27: 35 awards, 24 at the $20,000 maximum, others $7,000-$12,500. Program runs on a two-year cycle (2024-25, 2026-27); next cycle expected to open late 2027/early 2028. Awards go to nonprofits, cities and DMOs marketing to out-of-state/fly-in visitors through SEA.
